title: PRP for skin and hair in Cairo
description: Considering PRP in Cairo for hair or skin? Learn why diagnosis comes first, how platelet-rich plasma is prepared and how the treated area is followed up.
h1: PRP for skin and hair in Cairo
answer: Platelet-rich plasma, or PRP, uses a preparation from a patient's own blood for selected scalp or skin concerns. At {{brand}} in New Cairo and Mohandessin, adults can discuss what PRP might offer for their particular diagnosis. Hair thinning and skin changes may need a different treatment or further investigation.
preparation: Mention blood disorders, anticoagulants and scalp infection. Do not stop prescribed medicines on your own.
howPerformed: If suitable, the team takes a blood sample, prepares the platelet-rich portion and treats the assessed area.
followup: Expect possible soreness at the blood draw and treatment sites. Follow advice on washing the skin or scalp and when to review any change.
risks: Bruising, bleeding and infection can occur. Improvement is uncertain and depends on the underlying cause.

faqs.a: Both the blood draw and the skin or scalp injections can sting.

faqs.q: Can I have treatment if my skin marks easily?
faqs.a: A history of prolonged irritation or dark marks affects planning. Tell the team how your skin healed after previous procedures so the method and timing can be assessed.
